title: Two Sum
prompt: Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to `target`. You may assume each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice. Return the answer in any order.

examples.explanation: Both elements are equal, showing that duplicate values at different indices can still form a valid pair as long as they aren't the same element used twice.

hints: Brute force checks every pair — that's O(n^2). Can you find a complement in O(1)?
As you iterate, what if you remembered every value you'd already seen, along with its index?
A hash map from value to index lets you check 'have I seen target - nums[i] before?' in one lookup.

solution.approach: Walk the array once. For each value, compute its complement (target - value) and check a hash map for it. If found, you have your pair. Otherwise, store the current value's index in the map and continue. This turns an O(n^2) pairwise check into a single O(n) pass.
